mechanism: Three sealed search housings, each with a twelve-tile floor representing the searched hour, return identical empty trays at the agent’s counter. Opening a housing (click or “Open the housings”) reveals how far each search carriage travelled: lane 1 reached 60 minutes and holds no incidents; lane 2 stopped at a scan-budget block at 40 minutes with an incident beyond it; lane 3 timed out at 10 minutes with a parted backend cable and two incidents ahead. “Return status and coverage” adds a physical coverage strip, cursor tab or error flag to each tray, so the difference becomes visible from the agent’s side without opening anything. Fixture definition: each floor tile is a five-minute partition; lane 2 exhausts a scan budget of eight partitions despite zero matches, with four partitions unsearched. This is not an ordinary result-count limit.
spatialBenefit: No sufficient benefit established: the retained three-housing illustration is a hidden timeline diagram. Omit from publication.
beyondVideoTest: Omit. Requested scope × available partition intersection is useful, but two independent categorical axes form an ordinary coverage grid. A third depth axis has no domain meaning here; hiding it behind a cover adds effort without evidence. Existing timelines also fail the gate. No speculative replacement GLB is claimed.

primaryActions: Open the housings / Close the housings
Return status and coverage / Return a bare list
pickTargets: Any part of a housing, lane, carriage, incident or tray toggles that lane’s lid
The agent figure moves the camera behind the agent
interaction.motion: Lids swing about 0.8 seconds; coverage markers grow in about 0.25 seconds. Reduced motion applies states instantly. Nothing moves before an action.

expectedObservations: Closed, the three trays are identical and empty.
Open, only lane 1’s scored line reaches the 60-minute mark; lanes 2 and 3 stop early with amber incidents beyond the stopping point.
With coverage returned, the tray strips match the carriage stopping points, lane 2 shows a cursor tab and lane 3 an error flag.
sourceGuide: content/concepts/tool-design.json (example, walkthrough step 3 and pitfalls: empty list after timeout, dropped pagination or coverage)
limitations: The tray markers are metaphors for status, coverage and cursor fields; they are illustrative application fields, not MCP requirements, matching the guide.
A client-side transport timeout that yields no tool result at all is not depicted.
Retry budgets and argument validation from the guide are outside this scene.
Lane order is fixed, so a reader may learn the lanes’ meaning by position. The lane coverage words engraved on the counter appear only after coverage is returned.
Opened lids are tall and can occlude parts of the scene from low rear angles.
